title: Mastery Course: Understanding Harm, Safety and Repair
importantNotice: Educational content only. Follow configured safeguarding and emergency procedures where immediate safety concerns arise.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate intention, behaviour, impact, responsibility and repair
Analyse harm using child-centred and evidence-aware reasoning
Create measurable accountability, repair and prevention plans
Apply learning to unfamiliar complex scenarios

modules.title: Advanced Foundations of Harm
modules.definition: Harm is an adverse effect on a child's physical, emotional, psychological, relational or developmental wellbeing caused by an action, pattern, omission or unsafe environment.

content.heading: Intention, behaviour and impact
content.teachingText: Intention describes purpose, behaviour describes what occurred and impact describes what the child experienced. Analysis considers all three while keeping safety central.

content.heading: Patterns and cumulative impact
content.teachingText: Repeated, unpredictable or unrepaired events may create cumulative impact even where individual events appear minor.

content.heading: Evidence-aware reflection
content.teachingText: Use observable behaviour, context, child response, protective action and follow-up. Do not diagnose or guess motives.

activity.instructions: Identify observable behaviour, possible impact, missing information and the safest next step.

aiFacilitator.opening: Separate known facts from inference before evaluating impact.

content.heading: Child-centred perspective
content.teachingText: Consider developmental needs, dependency, power differences, predictability and access to support.

content.heading: Supportive response
content.teachingText: Reduce stress, use calm language, listen without interrogation and affirm that the child is not responsible for adult behaviour.

activity.instructions: Map immediate needs, possible effects, protective factors and appropriate supports.

aiFacilitator.opening: Consider the child's experience without presenting possibilities as confirmed facts.
prompts: Which protective factor can be strengthened?

content.heading: Accountability
content.teachingText: Name the behaviour, recognise impact, avoid excuses, accept responsibility and follow through.

content.heading: Repair
content.teachingText: Repair combines acknowledgement, changed behaviour, respect for boundaries and consistent safety. It does not demand forgiveness.

content.heading: Trust
content.teachingText: Trust is supported by repeated observable action rather than promises alone.

activity.instructions: Write a statement containing acknowledgement, impact, responsibility, an immediate safety action and a measurable commitment.

aiFacilitator.opening: Turn insight into accountable language and measurable action.

content.heading: Triggers and choice points
content.teachingText: A trigger may explain a reaction but does not remove responsibility. Strong plans identify warnings, pause strategies, supports and safer alternatives.

content.heading: Progress measurement
content.teachingText: Use behavioural indicators such as reduced escalation, calm responses, completed check-ins and adherence to safety plans.

content.heading: Setback planning
content.teachingText: Anticipate setbacks and identify thresholds for additional professional support.

capstone.title: Integrated Safety and Repair Plan
capstone.instructions: Analyse an unfamiliar case and address observable facts, possible impact, immediate safety, accountability, repair, prevention, supports and progress measures.

aiFacilitator.opening: Transfer all course concepts to a new complex situation.

scenarioAssessment.situation: A parent repeatedly tells a distressed child to stop crying and toughen up.
scenarioAssessment.question: Which response best demonstrates understanding and safety?

choices.text: Continue because emotional toughness builds resilience
Acknowledge the feeling, respond calmly and help identify the child's need
Ignore the child until the emotion passes

answerKey.explanation: It validates emotion and supports regulation.

scenarioAssessment.situation: A child becomes quiet and anxious when adult voices rise after repeated conflict.
scenarioAssessment.question: What should happen first?

choices.text: Restore calm, move conflict away and provide a safe check-in
Ask the child which adult is right
Say there is nothing to worry about
Wait for proof of lasting impact

answerKey.explanation: It reduces exposure and provides support without burdening the child.

rationales.B: Places the child in the dispute.

scenarioAssessment.situation: A parent recognises repeated angry reactions have affected their child and wants to rebuild trust.
scenarioAssessment.question: Which plan best demonstrates accountability and repair?

choices.text: Explain stress and ask the child to move on
Apologise once and promise it will never happen again
Name behaviour and impact, use a de-escalation plan, respect boundaries and review progress

answerKey.explanation: It integrates acknowledgement, safety, boundaries and sustained change.

knowledgeQuiz.question: What distinguishes impact from intention?
options: Impact is what the child experienced
knowledgeQuiz.explanation: Impact concerns effect or experience; intention concerns purpose.

knowledgeQuiz.question: Which commitment is measurable?
options: I will pause, lower my voice and check in after conflict

knowledgeQuiz.question: What comes first after immediate distress?
Which statement minimises impact?
options: I can see this affected you
It was not a big deal

knowledgeQuiz.question: What best indicates repair?
knowledgeQuiz.explanation: Repair is shown through sustained safer action.

assessmentAndMarking.criticalRequirement: Safety Prioritisation must be at least 70 percent. Unsafe recommendations cannot be offset by a high overall score.

remediationRules.action: Assign targeted review and one reassessment
Lock completion, replay safety content and require a new scenario assessment
Give corrective feedback and require a revised response

aiTeacher.name: SafeSteps Mastery Facilitator
aiTeacher.role: Trauma-informed educational facilitator and competency assessor
boundaries: Follow safeguarding procedures for immediate safety concerns
openingScript: Welcome to Understanding Harm, Safety and Repair at mastery level.
We will focus on accurate recognition, child-centred safety, accountable repair and measurable change.
You may pause at any time.

feedbackTemplates.mastery: You identified behaviour, impact, safety and measurable change.
feedbackTemplates.competent: Your response is safe. Add one observable progress measure.
feedbackTemplates.developing: Revisit the child's possible experience and state the immediate safety action.
feedbackTemplates.unsafe: Reframe around adult responsibility, emotional safety and a specific safer action.

markingAlgorithm.requiredEvidence: Reference the learner's wording for each awarded criterion
